opportunity: varnode_flags::indirectonly has two readers in the merged tree -- HighVariable::has_name (variable.rs) and Merge::merge_test_adjacent (merge.rs) -- and NO writer: Funcdata::markIndirectOnly / checkIndirectUse (funcdata_varnode.cc:801-858) were never ported and ActionMarkIndirectOnly shipped as a documented no-op although universal_sched already scheduled it one slot ahead of ActionMergeAdjacent. So is_indirect_only() answered false everywhere and both readers took the strictly-more-conservative branch: kuna refused every speculative merge with an illegal input, including the ones upstream allows.
root_cause: Both refusals are about an ILLEGAL INPUT -- an input Varnode ActionDirectWrite never reached, i.e. the leftover entry value of a frame slot the function overwrites before it reads. Refusing the merge is the right default (an uninitialized value must not be printed as a real one); upstream's exception is that when EVERY reader in the def-set is a plain CPUI_INDIRECT the leftover value is not read at all, so there is nothing to print wrongly. That exception needed the flag nothing wrote.
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-indirectonly.xml (the sound direction: `take` changes off->on, the directly-read counterexample `keep` must not) + tests/stages/kuna-indirectonly-escape.xml (the unsound direction; its first pass runs the DEFAULT, so flipping the shipped default turns it red) + 8 unit tests in kuna_indirectonly/tests.rs

census.method: throwaway KUNA_IO_DEBUG instrumentation in mark_indirect_only, release build, kuna decompile-all over the decbench stripped coreutils binaries (docs/features/indirectonly/census.txt); reverted before the shipped commit
census.finding: no flagged input is also `unaffected`, so HighVariable::has_name's indirectonly branch never fires on x86-64 ELF and removes no declaration; the live consumer is Merge::merge_test_adjacent

corpus_sweep.method: kuna decompile-all, default (off) vs --option indirectonly on; script docs/features/indirectonly/corpus-sweep.sh, classifier classify-escape.py, full output corpus-escape-classification.txt
corpus_sweep.slice_set: ls sort grep gzip diff bzip2 find tar at O0+O2; kmod e2fsck dpkg dpkg-query dash bash at O0+O2+O2-noinline

hand_settled.evidence: every access to the [rsp+0x18..0x2c] out-param block is a lea or a load; the function contains no store to any of those slots, and the ON arm emits `S[stack-0x1428] &= 0xff;`
`989d: mov r14d,DWORD PTR [rsp+0x28]` is the only reference to that slot in the whole function and it is a load; `97c9: lea r13,[rsp+0x20]` is the object handed to `9964: call e270`
`5922: mov [rsp+0x40],rdx` / `5927: mov [rsp+0x48],rax` -- the machine fills the struct and the OFF arm drops both stores
`43076..43085: add [rbp-0x218],1 / sub rax,[rbp-0x218] / mov [rbp-0x200],rax` is exactly the hunk
[rbp-0x40] is stored at 2021c and at 20307 (the loop increment read back at 202f4) -- both hunk statements
[rbp-0x48] is stored at 16b08 and incremented in memory at 16b7c (`add QWORD PTR [rbp-0x48],0x4`), which is the `&S[stack-0x50][1]` hunk

corpus_sweep.withdrawn_claim: The first round reported `0 BUG hunks` over 16 slices. That claim is withdrawn: its classifier had no escape predicate, and bzip2 -O2 sub_3890 -- inside that original 16-slice set -- is confirmed wrong output.
corpus_sweep.note: ESCAPE-CANDIDATE is not a verdict. Both directions of the merge look identical in the emitted C; only the disassembly separates a restored store from a fabricated one.
corpus_sweep.finding: 24 of the 27 changed functions write an escaped frame slot at a statement the OFF arm does not have, so no subset of the hunks is certified safe by the emitted C alone.
corpus_sweep.hand_settled_tally: 6 settled: 2 BUG (both -O2, the value lives in a register for its whole lifetime), 4 FIX (three of them -O0, where the variable really is on the frame)
corpus_sweep.stack_comment_mapping: the printed `// stack - X` is the rbp displacement minus 8; confirmed on the stage fixture, where `stack - 0xc8` is `-0xc0(%rbp)`

typesweep.command: scripts.decbench.typesweep --option indirectonly off --opt O0 --opt O2 --opt O2-noinline --project coreutils grep gzip diffutils bzip2 findutils tar shadow
typesweep.note: the option ships default-OFF, so `base` is the shipped default (off) and `test` is the option turned on; the measurement is symmetric and the arms are numerically identical
typesweep.control_identical_variables: 10739 functions byte-identical in both arms, 0 scored differently

speed_interleaved.method: off/on interleaved, min-of-N (the batched-median form above is contention-biased on this box: it read +16.8% on a loaded machine and +3.4% on a quiet one for the same build)

default_off_reason: The lifted merge_test_adjacent refusal is sound only when the illegal input is the DESTINATION of the copy (the machine really does store into the frame slot). When it is the SOURCE -- the machine loads an escaped frame slot into a register and mutates the register -- the merge makes the emitted C mutate the slot, fabricating a store a later call handed the enclosing object can read. A CPUI_INDIRECT is attached only where the storage is still live in the SSA, so a slot whose last read precedes the loop carries no INDIRECT at any later call and the cover-intersection test has nothing to intersect. Stock Ghidra 12.1.2 emits the same fabricated store on the same input (docs/features/indirectonly/counterexample.md), so this is an upstream defect the port inherits faithfully rather than a porting error; kuna declines to inherit it by default.

counterexample.synthetic: walk.S -- an object built on the frame, filled through its address by three calls, its count loaded into r14d and counted down in the register, its address then passed to a fourth call that reads the count
counterexample.roundtrip: both emitted bodies compiled against the same lib.c: walk_off prints `a_done sees n=3`, walk_on prints `a_done sees n=-1`
counterexample.ghidra_12_1_2: local_30 = local_30 + -1; -- identical fabricated store (analyzeHeadless + DecompInterface)

default_off_evidence.default_equals_origin_main: byte-identical decompile-all over ls-O2, tar-O2, bzip2-O2, kmod-O2-noinline, e2fsck-O0, bash-O2 against a separately built 83830e86
